title: Comparison maps for a change of coefficients
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings, with coefficient
changes $a_X\colon\Lambda_X\to\Lambda'_X$ and derived extensions of scalars
$T^X=L(\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X})$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]). For a morphism of schemes
$f\colon X\to Y$ write $f^*$, $f_*$ for the pullback and pushforward of module objects over
$\Lambda$ resp. $\Lambda'$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]), $Lf^*$, $Rf_*$ for their
derived functors ([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]), $j_!$ for the extension by zero along
an open immersion $j\colon U\to X$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]), and, when $f$ admits a
compactification, $Rf_!=R(g_*)\circ D(i_!)$ for the chosen compactification $f=g\circ i$
($i$ an open immersion, $g$ proper; [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]). Restriction and
extension of scalars $\operatorname{Res}$, $\operatorname{Ext}$ are those of
[sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

The *comparison maps* between the change of coefficients and the six functors are the following
natural transformations; all of them are produced formally, as conjugates and mates, from the
fact that restriction of scalars commutes with pushforward,
$\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}\circ f_*\cong f_*\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$, and with pullback,
$\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ f^*\cong f^*\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}$.

- **Extension by zero.** For every open immersion $j\colon U\to X$, an isomorphism
  $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}\circ j_!\cong j_!\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{a_U}$ and an isomorphism
  $T^X\circ D(j_!)\cong D(j_!)\circ T^U$ of functors
  $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})$ on the unbounded derived categories.

Assume moreover that $a$ is *flat*: for every scheme $X$ the extension of scalars
$\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}=\Lambda'_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}-$ is exact, i.e. $\Lambda'_X$ is flat
over $\Lambda_X$. Then:

- **(Pull)** an isomorphism $T^X\circ Lf^*\cong Lf^*\circ T^Y$ of functors
  $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})$, on the unbounded derived categories;
- **(Push)** a natural transformation $T^Y\circ Rf_*\to Rf_*\circ T^X$ of functors
  $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_Y})$, not an isomorphism in general;
- **(Shriek)** for $f$ admitting a compactification, a natural transformation
  $T^Y\circ Rf_!\to Rf_!\circ T^X$, namely (Push) for the proper part $g$ followed by the
  extension-by-zero isomorphism for the open part $i$; it is an isomorphism whenever (Push) for
  $g$ is an isomorphism.

The underived analogues $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}\circ f^*\cong f^*\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Y}$
and $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Y}\circ f_*\to f_*\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ exist without the
flatness assumption.

proof.text: Fix $a$ and $f$ as in the statement. The formal constructions used below are the restriction/transport square of [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square], whose components are identities on underlying objects by [lem-sfb-comap-mapmod-square-underlying], and conjugation and mates of [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso] and [def-sfb-mate-push-hom]. Conjugation is applied to composite adjunctions, so its output is an isomorphism; taking a mate alone supplies a transformation. For pullback the invertible-vertical scalar square is [def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso]; for the linear extension by zero the restriction comparison is [def-sfb-projection-formula-comap]. These specify the formal operations, including their directions, used in the following constructions.

Let $U_W=\operatorname{Res}_{a_W}$ and $E_W=\operatorname{Ext}_{a_W}$. The pushforward coefficient square of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] commutes. Substituting it into the restriction/transport square gives the natural isomorphism $c:U_Y f_*^{\Lambda'}\cong f_*^\Lambda U_X$ of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso]. The pushforwards here are the composites defined in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], so the square applies to exactly these functors. Define underived (Pull) by conjugating $c$ along $E_W\dashv U_W$ ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) and $f^*\dashv f_*$ for both coefficient rings. This gives $E_X f^*_{\Lambda}\cong f^*_{\Lambda'}E_Y$, with the convention fixed by [def-sfb-pull-iso]. Define underived (Push) to be its prescribed mate of $c$: its component is
$$E_Yf_*^\Lambda M\xrightarrow{E_Yf_*^\Lambda\eta^X_M}E_Yf_*^\Lambda U_XE_XM\xrightarrow{E_Yc^{-1}_{E_XM}}E_YU_Yf_*^{\Lambda'}E_XM\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^Y}f_*^{\Lambda'}E_XM.$$
Here $\eta^X$ and $\varepsilon^Y$ are the coefficient adjunction unit and counit. This is [def-sfb-push-hom]. Naturality follows from that of these three transformations. No exactness of $E_W$ is used.

source.place: Pushforward and pullback, first sentence and conjugate/mate constructions

proof.text: For the inverse-image square, apply [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] separately to the arbitrary condensed rings $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$: both vertical maps $\alpha_f$ and $\alpha'_f$ are invertible. Thus no restriction to the listed adic coefficient rings is being imposed. The invertible-square construction of step 1 gives the restriction/pullback isomorphism $U_X f^*_{\Lambda'}\cong f^*_{\Lambda}U_Y$ of [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso]. Use its levelwise version [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] on the unbounded categories. This is the right-adjoint comparison used for the open-immersion construction below and is available without flatness of $a$.

source.place: Pushforward and pullback, invertibility and levelwise comparison

proof.text: Now assume the stated flatness at every scheme $W$. It implies that $E_W$ preserves finite limits, so [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-preserves-homology] applies; [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives] gives preservation of K-injective complexes by $U_W$. Use [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso] to obtain $\bar c:D(U_Y)Rf_*^{\Lambda'}\cong Rf_*^{\Lambda}D(U_X)$ on unbounded categories. Define derived (Pull) to be its conjugate along $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $T^W\dashv D(U_W)$, supplied by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. This is the isomorphism of [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso]. Define derived (Push) as in [def-sfb-derived-push-hom]: apply the three-arrow formula of step 2 with $E_W,U_W,c,f_*$ replaced by $T^W,D(U_W),\bar c,Rf_*$. Its source is $T^Y Rf_*^{\Lambda}$ and its target is $Rf_*^{\Lambda'}T^X$. Conjugation gives an isomorphism for (Pull), whereas the mate formula does not assert invertibility for (Push).

For an open immersion $j:U\to X$, the linearization comparison in step 1 yields the restriction/extension-by-zero isomorphism [def-sfb-comap-open-immersion-shriek-iso]. For extension of scalars, use the restriction/pullback comparison of step 3 at $j$. Its conjugate along the coefficient adjunctions and $j_!\dashv j^*$ is, by [def-sfb-open-immersion-shriek-iso], $E_Xj_!^{\Lambda}\cong j_!^{\Lambda'}E_U$. The adjunction and exactness of $j_!$ are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. At the derived level use [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso], which supplies the conjugate along $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ and $T\dashv D(U)$, including these ambient derived adjunctions, and gives $T^XD(j_!^{\Lambda})\cong D(j_!^{\Lambda'})T^U$. Its statement explicitly applies to every coefficient morphism without flatness. We use this derived conjugate, rather than deriving a composite of nonexact scalar-extension functors without a comparison theorem.

Retain flatness and choose the same compactification $X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{g}Y$ for both rings. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], $Rf_!^\Lambda=Rg_*^\Lambda D(i_!^\Lambda)$ and likewise for $\Lambda'$. Whisker derived (Push) for $g$ on the right by $D(i_!^\Lambda)$, then whisker the isomorphism of step 5 for $i$ on the left by $Rg_*^{\Lambda'}$. Define (Shriek) as their composite, with the canonical reassociations:
$$T^Y Rg_*^\Lambda D(i_!^\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Push}_g}Rg_*^{\Lambda'}T^Z D(i_!^\Lambda)\xrightarrow{Rg_*^{\Lambda'}(\sigma_i)}Rg_*^{\Lambda'}D(i_!^{\Lambda'})T^X.$$
This is precisely [def-sfb-derived-lower-shriek-hom], and its endpoints are $T^YRf_!^\Lambda$ and $Rf_!^{\Lambda'}T^X$. The transformation is attached to the chosen compactification; no independence assertion is required.

source.place: (Shriek), definition expanded as the two whiskered factors

proof.text: If derived (Push) for $g$ is an isomorphism, the criterion [lem-sfb-derived-lower-shriek-hom-iso] applies. Explicitly, write the two factors of step 6 as $u$ and $v$. Then $u^{-1}$ is the component of $\mathrm{Push}_g^{-1}$ evaluated on $D(i_!)$, and $v^{-1}=Rg_*^{\Lambda'}(\sigma_i^{-1})$. Functoriality gives $v^{-1}v=vv^{-1}=1$, and the inverse of $vu$ is $u^{-1}v^{-1}$, with inverse associators inserted in reverse order. Both inverse equations follow by cancellation. Thus (Shriek) is invertible under exactly the stated hypothesis on the proper part.

split_report.summary: Reused the existing formal and coefficient comparison nodes; specified mates and conjugates, the chosen-compactification composite, and its inverse. Replaced the restricted Cartesian-coefficients citation by the general alpha-isomorphism lemma. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Formal input: step 1; pushforward and pullback: steps 2–3; derived comparisons: step 4; extension by zero: step 5; Shriek: steps 6–7.

tool_uses.why: General invertibility for an arbitrary condensed ring is needed in the unit pullback square; sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients states only listed admissible coefficients. This generic coefficient lemma preserves the unit route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q127-a17acfaba (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the unit, the 5-paragraph blueprint proof (main-20261015) and the statements of all 34 cited nodes. The statement is identical to the blueprint's, there are no new nodes and no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the unit realized fields map paragraphs 1–5 to steps 1/2–3/4/5/6–7. The live item is still imported and there is no repair or re-split note. The directions of the underived and derived conjugates and mates match def-sfb-pull-iso/push-hom and derived-pull-iso/push-hom: Pull is E_X f^*≅f'^*E_Y and Push is E_Y f_*→f'_*E_X via unit, c^{-1} and counit. The coefficient-change squares instantiate def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square and def-sfb-extend-comap-iso-of-iso correctly. Flatness gives the finite-limit hypotheses of the homology and K-injective lemmas. The extension-by-zero conjugates need no flatness, which I checked (j_! of a K-flat complex is K-flat). The Shriek composite has the right whiskered endpoints for the same chosen compactification. The one change replaces sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients, whose clause (1) covers only admissible rings, with lem-sfb-alpha-iso (any condensed ring, reviewed N0 pass, proof c_f at Λ). This is correct, and I accept that tool use because the base citation was already off-route and the lemma is a generic black box. Edge cases f=id, a=id, U=∅ and non-flat Z→Z/2 are all fine. Advisory: the report's attachment of AddCommGrpCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution to lem-sfb-abelian-functorial-flat-resolution looks right, but it sits at live Basic.lean:150, not 148.
